notes: UNARMED. No verified non-zero pass@k baseline has been measured yet. Per Requirement 15.7 the eval pass@k gate is armed ONLY after a non-zero baseline is established (at or after M1) by the REAL Simulator oracle (iverilog + vvp). The prime directive forbids fabricating a baseline: a gate may be armed against a non-zero baseline only if that baseline was measured by the deterministic oracle, never guessed. While unarmed, the TypeScript and Python lint/type/unit/property jobs are the merge authority (Req 15.7) and this gate never blocks. The gate entry still runs the REAL ratcheting decision path (app/eval gate CLI -> decideEvalGate) so it is ready to block the moment a real baseline is recorded here.
armingProcedure: 1. Provision a host with the real EDA toolchain installed (iverilog + vvp) and a Python interpreter that can import tool_runner_worker.
2. Wire the real Eval_Harness loop-runner adapter (task 19.4) so the harness drives the fixed VerilogEval/RTLLM subset through the Verification_Loop and the real oracle under student-session caps.
3. Run the harness over the fixed subset with the pinned reproducibility config (fixed seed, temperature, sampleCount) and read aggregatePassAtK[k] for the k below (Req 15.10).

4. Record that measured non-zero pass@k as "baseline" (0, 1], set "floor" strictly below it as the absolute catastrophic-failure floor (Req 15.8), keep "tolerance" sized to absorb only residual measurement noise (Req 15.11), set "armed": true, and fill "provenance" with the tool versions, host, commit, seed, and sampleCount that produced the number.

5. Commit this file. The gate is now armed and will block a merge when the measured pass@k drops strictly below baseline - tolerance, or is at/below the floor (Req 15.4, 15.8). The baseline only ratchets up thereafter, except by an explicit reviewed lowering (Req 15.9).
